```plato
//==
// # library Polynomials
//
// Closed-form evaluation of the low-degree power-basis polynomials and of the
// cubic spline bases (Bezier, Hermite, Catmull-Rom), plus their first and second
// derivatives.
//
// The coefficients / control values are typed `INumerical`, which inherits
// IAdditive (a + b, a - b, Zero) and IScalable (v * scalar, v / scalar) — exactly
// the operations a polynomial in a scalar variable needs. So a
// single definition serves Number, Vector2D, Vector3D, Point deltas, Color, and
// every quantity type. The variable itself is
// always a plain `Number`; `INumerical` deliberately does NOT give
// IMultiplicative, so `value * value` is unavailable here and every product with
// the parameter is written as a scalar multiply.
//
// These are the base case the curve/surface layer is missing: an `Eval` on
// CubicBezier2D/3D, HermiteCurve2D/3D or CatmullRomCurve2D/3D is a one-line call
// into the corresponding function below.
//
// Not repeated here: `Barycentric` (already generic on INumerical in
// algebra.library.plato) and `SmoothStep`/`SmootherStep` (Number-concrete
// shaping functions, also in algebra.library.plato).
//
// Conventions: coefficients come first in descending-power (school) order,
// matching the QuadraticPolynomial/CubicPolynomial/QuarticPolynomial types of
// `polynomials.types.plato`; the variable is last. Bezier/Hermite/Catmull-Rom
// parameters t are in [0, 1].

library Polynomials
{
    //==
    // # Power-basis polynomials

    // m*x + b. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_equation
    Linear(m: INumerical, b: INumerical, x: Number): INumerical
        => m * x + b;
```
